newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil losing soy market share to Argentina-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil losing soy market share to Argentina-Safras.

text.p: Brazil's soybean processing industry is losing market share to its Mercosur partner Argentina which benefits from lower costs and a better tax structure, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.

"Brazil is losing export market share for soymeal and soyoil to Argentina and is characterized by the export of beans, with a consequent loss of added value for the country's economy," Safras said in a weekly report.

Farmers in Argentina's key soybean growing regions have lower production costs than in Brazil and processing plants are usually placed near producing areas, meaning industry has access to cheaper grains, it said.

In addition, port costs were $2-3 per tonne on average, compared to $8-12 in Brazil and loading was rapid, while at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua vessels waited for up to 30 days during the peak of harvesting in March and April, it said.
Argentina's tax structure also favors exports of soymeal and soyoil which benefit from zero percent value-added tax, as opposed to 3.5 percent on soybeans.

"This tax difference was lower in Brazil until 1996, but it existed in the sense that the ICMS (export tax) rates were 13 percent, 11.1 percent and eight percent respectively for soybeans, meal and oil," Safras said.
The abolition of the tax in September 1996 meant the differential disappeared and it was now more profitable to export soybeans rather than soy products, it added.

Brazil's crushing capacity remained stable at 30 million tonnes in the last five years while in Argentina, it jumped from 14 to 21 million tonnes in the same period with a projected growth to 28 million tonnes in the next two years, Safras said.
